The official BPAS Plan Approval Manual describes an authenticated architect workflow with project creation, applicant/consultant and plot/building details, document attachment, geolocation, application-type selection, drawing upload and AutoDCR scrutiny, NOC/document attachment, challan and final submission.

The current BPAS downloads page publicly lists a Plan Approval manual, Plan Sanction checklist, Schedule-II prescribed application, Schedule-III supervision form, professional/owner affidavits, bonds and Nambike Nakshe/Single Plot Approval forms.

The public Suvarna Paravanige procedure PDF describes zonal-office residential building-plan sanction for a site area up to 4,000 sq ft, up to four dwelling units and up to 15 m height, with online filing plus hard-copy records/drawings, scrutiny/processing charge, inspection, document/drawing verification, demand note, fee receipt and approval/rejection steps.

The official site-inspection procedure document states inspection schedules of within 7 days for head-office plan sanction and within 3 days for zonal-office plan sanction, with inspection-report publication within 48 hours and 24 hours respectively.

A BBMP/Karnataka administrative-reforms report records a Sakala time limit of 3 days where online data is available and 7 days where it is not for issue of birth, still-birth, and death certificates.

The historic BBMP manual describes Form 6 and a free first extract for information reported within 21 days, and a BBMP/Karnataka report records a 3-day online-data/7-day non-online-data Sakala target; current applicability is not established.

Karnataka's official Chief Registrar/e-JanMa material states that deaths in urban local-body and BBMP areas are registered in e-JanMa by Health Officers and Health Inspectors, while deaths in private hospitals are reported by the concerned private hospital to the respective Registrar.
Official Karnataka e-JanMa material says BBMP/urban deaths are registered by Health Officers and Health Inspectors and private hospitals report deaths to the respective Registrar.
Section 25A allows a person aggrieved by a Registrar action or order to appeal to the District Registrar within thirty days in the prescribed form and manner.
Section 25A allows a person aggrieved by a District Registrar action or order to appeal to the Chief Registrar within thirty days in the prescribed form and manner.

Section 7(2) requires a Registrar to enter birth/death information given under sections 8 or 9 for events occurring in the Registrar's jurisdiction, and section 7(3) requires an office in the local area for which the Registrar is appointed.
The linked Karnataka death-certificate manual instructs a user to retain the generated acknowledgement/reference.

The BBMP Revenue Department's published Khatha Services page lists a previous title deed or government-agency possession certificate, current-year tax-paid receipt, will, original death certificate, Form 15 Encumbrance Certificate, and—where the will is unregistered—a notarised family tree and family NOC for Khatha Transfer through inheritance with a will.

The BBMP Revenue Department's published Khatha Services page lists a sale deed, current-year tax-paid receipt, and an Encumbrance Certificate in Form 15 from the sale-deed date to the current date for Khatha Transfer through sale deed.

The public e-Aasthi citizen instructions say mobile/OTP login is used to see or download Draft eKhata; the draft is issued according to the existing BBMP Property Tax Register; additional information for Final eKhata includes a registered deed, Aadhaar-based eKYC, SAS Property Tax Application Number, property photo, and documents proving A-Khata, with an encumbrance certificate noted when immediate sale or transfer is planned.

Rule 10 of the BBMP Property Tax Assessment, Recovery and Management Rules, 2024 specifies Form 21 for an inheritor, survivor, or successor after death, and Form 22 for a registered deed where the Sub-Registrar intimation slip has not reached BBMP; Form 22 requires a certified copy of the registered deed.

The public e-Khata Application Status page accepts an EPID, displays stage/from/received/sent/sent-to/status/remarks columns, and publishes waiting-list and online-status guidance together with eKhata helpline 9480683695.

Rule 10(3) of the BBMP Property Tax Assessment, Recovery and Management Rules, 2024 states that if no objection is received within fifteen days of service of notice, the Assistant Revenue Officer or authorised officer certifies the mutation and the e-Khata order is issued in Form 24.
The public eKhata Application Status view displays No Data Available when no result row is present; this does not diagnose an invalid EPID or an ownership state.

The public eKhatha Application Status page exposes an EPID input with SEARCH STATUS and RESET, shows status/routing/date/remarks headings, and renders the literal default row `No Data Available` when no EPID is entered; it also publishes waiting-list guidance and helpline 9480683695.

HP Gas's current FAQ says that for an out-of-town transfer, the current distributor issues a TV and refunds the SV deposit after surrender of cylinders and regulator; the TV is valid for one year, and the Domestic Gas Consumer Card should be retained for endorsement at the new location.

IndianOil's current Indane FAQ says that an out-of-town move requires surrender of the cylinder and regulator to the current distributor, who prepares a TV and refunds the equipment deposit; the customer is directed to a distributor at the new place for future service.

IndianOil's current Indane FAQ says that for a same-town move outside the present distributor's service area, the old distributor prepares a TTV against the original SV, and the receiving distributor uses proof of residence, TTV and DGCC booklet to prepare a TSV and provide a new consumer number.

HPCL's current public FAQ describes within-city or adjoining-city transfer using an e-CTA authorization code with SV and new-distributor enrollment, while an outside-town transfer uses a TV, equipment surrender/refund and reconnection at the new place.

IndianOil's current public FAQ describes three Indane branches: same distributor area uses new-address proof for a record change; same-town transfer uses SV, TTV, DGCC and TSV without equipment surrender; out-of-town transfer uses SV/TSV and DGCC with equipment surrender for a TV and later reconnection.

For a move within the same town where the present distributor does not service the new address, the manual says to approach the old distributor with the original Subscription Voucher for a Transfer Termination Voucher/City Transfer Advise Out, then approach the new distributor with residence proof, TTV/CTA Out and DGCC booklet; the new distributor prepares TSV/CTA In and provides a new consumer number.

The published path branches on whether the new address remains in the same distributor's operating area; if not, the manual describes a same-town transfer using old- and new-distributor voucher steps.

For same-town service-area change, the manual says old distributor uses the original Subscription Voucher to prepare TTV/CTA Out; the customer then presents residence proof, TTV/CTA Out and DGCC booklet to the receiving distributor, which prepares TSV/CTA In and provides a new consumer number.

The current Kaveri Marriage Registration FAQ says three witnesses are required and each must be over 18; it lists one mandatory age-proof item (birth certificate, SSLC, school cumulative record or doctor certificate), one mandatory address-proof item (ration card, passport, driving licence, employee ID, bank passbook or voter ID), one identity-proof item (including PAN, passport, driving licence, bank passbook, ration card, Aadhaar, voter ID or employee ID), a mandatory wedding invitation plus one marriage-venue receipt/other relevant proof, and a photo limit of 2 MB in PNG format.

The current Kaveri Marriage Registration FAQ says a Hindu Marriage Certificate is applied for post-marriage; offline Hindu Marriage Aadhaar is not mandatory, online Hindu Marriage Aadhaar is mandatory, and an online Hindu Marriage application need not be submitted by visiting the Sub-Registrar office.

The current Kaveri Marriage Registration FAQ says that for Special Marriage of Other Forms, online processing requires Aadhaar for the bride, bridegroom and all three witnesses plus eKYC; offline processing does not require Aadhaar and requires personal appearance to submit the signed application before the Sub-Registrar; online applicants can download the final certificate after approval and offline certificates are issued at the office after document/party verification.

The public Kaveri Marriage Registration dashboard exposes a date range, a Sub Registrar Offices List containing Bengaluru entries such as Kengeri, Banasawadi, Ganganagar, Indiranagar, Shivajinagar and Yeshwanthpura, and real-time dashboard labels; it showed PSGA time limit 3 Day(s) on 2026-08-31.

BESCOM's public FAQ lists document classes including registered sale/gift/partition deed, khata, latest tax receipt, registered lease, occupancy certificate, solar-water-heater compliance, identity/address and other conditional technical or undertaking documents; the eligibility page requires prescribed documents to be verified with originals and lists power-supply agreement and contractor completion/test report conditions.

The blank JVS Document Upload stage shows `Upload Documents - Please upload any one of the document for mandatory (*) category`, accepted extensions `.JPEG, .JPG, .BMP, .TIF, .TIFF, .JPE, .JFIF, .PDF, .GIF`, `Max Total Upload Size : 4 MB`, DigiLocker file and Document Status columns, Choose File for Identity Proof*, Proof of Ownership*, Geo-Tagged building photo* and Completion Certificate, a Get Aadhaar from Digilocker link, and a final Submit.

The JVS document table labels Identity Proof* with `Photo copy of PAN Card/Driving License/Passport/Aadhar Card/Voter ID*`, Proof of Ownership* with `Photo copy of the Sales deed, Khata certificate, Tax paid certificate.`, Geo-Tagged building photo* with `Upload full building photo along with LAT LONG`, and Completion Certificate with `Completion-cum test report along with wiring diagram`.

BESCOM's home page displays power supply within 24 hours after requisite-fee payment for qualifying domestic LT-1 and commercial LT-3 consumers up to the fast-track load limit where no line extension is needed; it also displays a Bengaluru EODB new-connection target of 7 days without RoW and 15 days with RoW for stated LT/HT load bands.
BESCOM's public New Connection Tracker exposes a required Request ID or Account ID input and a Submit control; the same public page displays a 1912 help label.

KERC's 2022 consumer-rights regulation says an owner or occupier files the electricity-supply application with prescribed fee/charges, and an online submission through the licensee's web portal or mobile app must generate an acknowledgement with a registration number; a complete application is deemed received on that acknowledgement date.

BESCOM’s public FAQ says that if money is debited but payment acknowledgement is not generated, do not pay again for the same bill; wait 24 hours for Bill Desk to confirm with the bank and update payment, or use the published Bill Desk telephone 080-25586664 and Customer Care 1912.
The public BESCOM New Connection Tracker exposes `Request ID*`, an `OR` separator, `Account ID*` and a `Submit` button.

The BBMP Revenue checklist lists a sale deed, current-year property-tax receipt, and Form 15 encumbrance certificate from the sale-deed date to the current date for khatha transfer through sale deed.

The BBMP Revenue checklist publishes separate inheritance-with-will and inheritance-without-will branches, including prior title/possession evidence, current tax receipt, death evidence, family-tree/NOC material in stated cases, and an encumbrance certificate.

The current public e-Aasthi EC-upload page says an application will not be processed if its registered deed number is not in the submitted encumbrance certificate.

BESCOM's current Janasnehi page states that Name Change and some related services are within 24 hours.
BESCOM's public tracker requests the request ID sent by SMS.

BBMP's public new-registration guide says to open Trade License/New Registration, enter mandatory fields, continue, upload owner consent letter or lease agreement and electricity bill, send an OTP, choose the number of years and proceed to payment.
The official procedure says an authorised officer sets the inspection date on the filing date and the maximum time set for inspection is within 3 working days, using a compliance checklist.

The official OTLS description says the case may produce a temporary application number/payment challan, use online or offline payment, pass through inspection/document verification and MoH/DHO/HO review, and reach final approval/license issue with status/download features.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Contract reconciliation
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: IND-9's older description has six roadblock labels, but the accepted v1 contract permits exactly `documentation`, `process`, and `infrastructure`. The ledger does not widen that enum.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Inline Result
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: The document passes the JSON Schema, and its 21 edges have claim references. Preserve the evidence-backed graph: 19 `partial`, one `unknown`, and one `verified` edge. In particular, the partial/unknown birth-workflow edges appropriately retain the stated limitation that the current BBMP transition, required fields, submission, payment, result, and tracking were not publicly observed. The statutory claims support the legal relationships, not a completed current municipal journey.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Scope and result
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: Audited `ledger/building-plan.json` against `ledger/schema.json` and `ledger/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md` only. The JSON validates against the supplied schema; IDs are unique, all checked links resolve, every non-`Unknown` claim has a source, and recorded dates are ISO-shaped.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Result
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: The ledger passes JSON-schema validation and all checked cross-record references resolve. The public journey consistently keeps individual record state, registrar, fee, timing, correction eligibility, and certificate outcome unknown. The observations below are visible documentation limitations, not release blockers.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Verdict: revise before relying on the graph
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: The JSON validates against `ledger/schema.json`; all IDs and cross-record references resolve, contradiction links that exist are reciprocal, IDs are unique, and the observed date values are ISO calendar-valid and no later than `meta.asOf`. Jurisdiction labels are appropriately Bengaluru/Karnataka for municipal claims and Karnataka for the statewide historic KERC material.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Material findings
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: Broken claim references in node details. Fourteen nested `checks`, `failureSignals`, or `recoveries` reference claim IDs that do not exist: `claim_ind32_automatic_mutation_entry`, `claim_ind32_pending_mutation_report_fields` (twice), `claim_ind32_payment_failure_recovery` (four times), `claim_ind32_public_search_inputs` (three times), `claim_ind32_ekhata_status_public_route` (three times), and `claim_ind32_missing_property_route` (twice). These records therefore lose their evidence linkage and violate reference integrity.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Inline Verdict

The JSON validates against the supplied schema; all IDs are unique, all checked cross-references resolve, all non-`Unknown` claims have a source, dates are ISO-shaped, and URLs are present. This is an evidence-quality audit, not a factual re-research.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Scope and result

This assesses the ledger’s stated evidence, not the live legal or portal position.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Result
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: The ledger passes JSON-schema validation and all checked cross-record references resolve. The public journey is appropriately explicit that route selection, eligibility, documents, demand, payment, inspection, and supply are not case outcomes. The observations below are visible documentation limitations, not release blockers.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Result
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: The IND-32 property-tax records parse cleanly and the audited claims, nested details, journey steps, dependencies, and top-level edges resolve to existing IDs. The reusable journey dependency from the pending-mutation report to application status is now retained as `edge_workflow_mutation_to_status_ind32`, with the same `unknown` status and claim linkage.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Scope and result
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: Audited `ledger/trade-license.json` against `ledger/schema.json` and `ledger/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md` only. The JSON validates against the supplied schema; all checked references resolve, IDs are unique, all non-`Unknown` claims cite at least one source, and recorded access dates are ISO-shaped.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Inline Result
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: The document passes the JSON Schema and all checked internal references resolve. Scenario path-node membership, edge endpoint scenario membership, and journey references are internally consistent. Preserve all 12 edges: eight `partial`, three `unknown`, and one `verified`. The three `unknown` account-transfer edges are evidence-backed by the inspected public Jaladhare/FAQ material and correctly state what was *not* observed; they should remain visible rather than be removed.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Result
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: The IND-32 water-connection records parse cleanly and their audited claims, nested details, journey steps, dependencies, and top-level edges resolve to existing IDs. Both journey dependencies are represented as top-level edges with matching endpoints, claim linkage, and status.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Verdict
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: Needs targeted correction before the exception journeys are treated as source-supported. The new Conditions-PDF claims are generally atomic, dated, linked, and appropriately cautious at Grade C/`partial`; direct public-interface observations are generally Grade B/`verified`; and the explicit Unknown claims properly have no sources. Reference-integrity checks found no dangling scenario, node, claim, source, roadblock, or journey references. The recorded NOC contradiction is reciprocal and contested. Exception nodes carry no `researchedNoSourceFound` markers, so there is no unsupported marker to remove.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Findings
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: Remove `roadblock_audit_death_certificate` (material integrity failure). Its `symptom` is a pasted audit report, including a purported scope, result, and unrelated identifiers such as `node_sale_deed` and `scenario_clean_sale`. It has no supporting claims. It is not an atomic user-visible blocker and its `unknown` status does not make the narrative evidence-backed.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Findings requiring correction or explicit disclosure
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: Normal-route evidence is tagged as the JVS scenario. `claim_ind44_electricity_normal_form_fields`, `claim_ind44_electricity_document_upload_boundary`, `claim_ind44_normal_form_controls`, `claim_ind44_normal_faq_route`, and `claim_ind44_normal_payment_boundary` all describe the normal route/form but carry only `scenario_ind32_electricity_jvs`. This misstates provenance and leaves the normal scenario without the evidence that purportedly supports it. The broad KERC timing, acknowledgement, escalation, and charge claims are likewise presented only as JVS evidence even where their wording is not JVS-specific.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Required corrections
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: Repair observation provenance before relying on the claims. `claim_ind45_missing_route_no_navigation` and `claim_ind45_pending_mutation_route_currently_blank` describe actions/outcomes on 2026-08-30, but cite only IND-32 sources accessed on 2026-08-28. The latter also records a second `/office/` URL absent from its source record. Add claim-specific 2026-08-30 observation sources (or update the cited source records with those exact observations and access date); otherwise remove the dated/action-result wording. `claim_ind45_draft_login_controls_visible` likewise says it was directly observed on 2026-08-30 while its only cited source is recorded as accessed 2026-08-28.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Required corrections
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: Repair dangling agencies (material). `roadblock_ind46_legacy_routes` names `agency_gba_trade_ind46` and `agency_bbmp_trade_ind46_legacy`; `roadblock_ind46_trade_outcome_boundary` names `agency_gba_trade_ind46`. None exists in `agencies`. Replace them with evidence-supported existing agencies or add real agency records; do not leave inferred current/legacy ownership.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Result
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: The JSON parses, IDs are unique, and the direct ID references checked for claims, sources, nodes, scenarios, and node-detail claim lists resolve. Every non-`Unknown` claim has at least one source. Those structural checks do not make the route or the displayed journey reliable: citation scope, claim atomicity, reciprocal evidence links, and scenario coverage are materially unsound.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Result
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: The IND-48 additions contain useful current primary-law and public-interface observations, but the ledger is not ready to present as a single coherent marriage journey. It currently mixes a legacy route graph with an IND-48 graph, duplicates sources and claims, and lets route-unknown citizen evidence appear as HMA evidence. The documented public record supports statutory route information and observed interface guidance; it does not support a case-specific Bengaluru application outcome, SRO allocation, or universal checklist.

auditorExcerpts.heading: Ship decision
auditorExcerpts.excerpt: Do not ship IND-49 as a single Bengaluru LPG journey. It can ship only as clearly separated, provider-specific public guidance with the case outcome hidden as Unknown. The current material does not determine a consumer's OMC, assigned distributor, service area, provider-specific document packet, eligibility, or transaction result.
